placements.why: This envelope is an observatory calibration report end to end — a prose confirmation plus a structured instrument/calibration log — and nothing in the existing (empty) strata covers organizational content of this shape. The org's own named strata set includes 'Calibration' as a top-level category; this is the first envelope whose content actually calls for minting it, so it is minted standalone with no parent required.
placements.title: Observatory calibration and verification practice as a distinct organizational category
placements.frame: Does this content report an instrument calibration or verification event or practice, as distinct from opportunity, strategy, product, architecture, organization, proof, or template concerns?

placements.title: Instrument calibration claims are grounded in verification against an external reference standard, not the instrument's own reading
placements.frame: Does this calibration event ground its claim in verification against a named external reference standard, and does that verification hold across the instrument's full operating range?
placements.why: src-1 states the calibration in prose and explicitly grounds it in verification 'against the June reference plates,' holding 'across the full observing band'; src-2 and src-3 restate the same instrument identity and calibration-against-reference-plates fact as structured log fields. The specific 88.4 MHz figure and the June plates are a one-time fact, but the underlying subject — that calibration claims at this observatory are validated by deference to an external reference standard rather than asserted from the instrument's own output — is a theme future calibration envelopes (other instruments, other reference sets) will keep feeding, so the fact is filed as support under a minted thematic leaf rather than given its own node. No existing narrative structure was available to reuse (graph structure supplied empty), so this is a genuine first mint rather than a paraphrase of something already present.
